metadata.title: Seed Annual Research Update Ledger
metadata.description: Every fact in the Seed app that has a vintage and can go stale, with where it lives, where it came from, how often the source republishes, and what to watch for. Reference document for the yearly data pass.

how_to_use.when: Run a full pass once a year, after the June DEFRA/DESNZ release (the single biggest input). Ember publishes in April and the UN SDG Report in July, so a July-August pass catches all three.
order: 1. Refresh carrier factors first (grid, gas) -- everything else multiplies through them.
2. Refresh transport modes (DEFRA release) and re-derive the transport sanity pins.
3. Refresh energy appliance averages and re-derive the energy sanity pins.
4. Re-read the food drift inputs only (the P&N anchor itself is a fixed 2018 study).
5. Reconcile impact_equivalencies.json against the datasets it mirrors -- this is where drift hides.
7. Update sdg_world_state from the new UN SDG Report.
8. Update last_reviewed here and record what moved.
rules: Every changed value needs a fresh verbatim quote, full URL and access date before it ships (AUDIT_ACTION_DATA.md sections 2 and 8).
Never average two figures on different statistics or boundaries (the D1 defect).
Re-derive the sanity-invariant pins after any value change; they are data pins, not truth claims, and several are thin by design.
A figure seen only in a search-engine summary may not enter sources[] -- re-fetch it in a browser first.
Physics-derived values (water heating, boiling) never need refreshing; only the assumptions around them (flow rate, delta-T, efficiency) can age.

volatility_scale.high: moves materially most years; always re-read
volatility_scale.medium: moves every few years; re-read annually, expect no change most passes
volatility_scale.fixed: a dated study or a standard; does not move -- see stable_do_not_rechase

items.title: Electricity grid carbon intensity (house factor)

source.name: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026
source.anchor_quote: from 533 grams of CO2 equivalent per kWh (gCO2e/kWh) in 2015 to 458 gCO2e/kWh in 2025

cross_check_source.name: IEA, Electricity 2026
cross_check_source.note: 435 g CO2/kWh for 2025, CO2-only. The 5.3% gap to Ember is CO2e scope. Do NOT average the two.

items.trend: falling ~3%/yr; IEA forecasts 360 g CO2/kWh by 2030
watch_for: Scope: must stay CO2e to match the rest of the app.
Ember revising prior years when it reprocesses.
A regionalisation decision superseding the single constant (see Plan/PDR_GRID_REGIONALISATION.md).
items.notes: Retired value was 386 g CO2/kWh, whose documented derivation ('midpoint of US 370 and UK 210') computed to 290 and did not reproduce it.

items.title: Natural gas combustion factor
items.vintage: DEFRA/DESNZ 2026 release (0.18231, Scope 1 combustion, Gross CV)

source.name: UK DEFRA/DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2026, flat-format spreadsheet

cross_check_source.name: 資源エネルギー庁 (METI), 都市ガス 13A
cross_check_source.note: 2.244 kgCO2/m3 at 45 MJ/m3 = 179.5 g/kWh; agrees with DEFRA to 1.4%

watch_for: Must stay Gross CV, combustion-only (no well-to-tank) for boundary parity with transport.
Gas composition barely changes; a large move means the wrong row was read.
items.notes: Best-corroborated number in the energy dataset. Cheapest check on this list.

items.title: Transport mode emission factors (27 modes)
items.current_value: 27 modes, DEFRA/DESNZ 2025 vintage unless a mode notes otherwise
watch_for: Known pending 2026 revisions not yet applied: coach +42%, national rail -13%, London Underground -44%, international rail +154%, UK BEV anchor to ~30 g/km.
Aggregator tables routinely mix vintages -- record the release year per figure.
Re-derive ALL section 6 sanity pins after any change; several flip under the 2026 numbers (coach vs national rail is documented as a deliberate non-invariant).

items.title: Battery electric vehicle factor
items.current_value: 73 g/km (PENDING rebase to 86 g/km under E1)
items.vintage: 0.188 kWh/km real-world consumption x house grid factor
items.release_cadence: consumption figure drifts slowly; recomputed whenever the grid factor moves
watch_for: This is the app's most visible cross-carrier number and has no gating equivalent to the energy dataset's carrier rule.
A UK user's true figure at DEFRA 2026 (131 g/kWh) is ~25 g/km -- the global factor overstates it ~3.4x. Flagged in Plan/PDR_GRID_REGIONALISATION.md section 1.2.

items.title: Aviation radiative-forcing multiplier

source.name: DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors methodology paper

items.release_cadence: annual, but the multiplier itself rarely moves
watch_for: Any change in the published central estimate; helicopter is deliberately combustion-only (low-altitude) and must not inherit it.

items.title: City-pair border and crossing status
items.current_value: 982 cities; CLOSED_BORDERS list and manual walls

source.name: GeoNames cities15000 (CC BY 4.0) + manual geopolitical screen

watch_for: Watchlist from RESEARCH_TRANSPORT.md appendix A.5: BJ-NE (2026-06 reopening accord was prospective), DZ-LY (conflicting sources), AM-TR (conditional on an unsigned treaty), ER-ET (fragile-ok), Rafah/Gaza, Sudan front line (Kordofan).
cities.json was edited in place, so a full regeneration backfills freed top-5 slots with new cities that must be border-screened.

items.title: Food emission factors (Poore & Nemecek via OWID)
items.current_value: 42 items, production-weighted means with supply-chain losses
items.vintage: P&N 2018 study; OWID grapher last updated 2019-10-08

source.name: Our World in Data, ghg-per-kg-poore grapher

items.release_cadence: the underlying study is fixed (2018); OWID reprocesses occasionally
watch_for: OWID switching the default statistic again (it moved from medians-without-losses to means-with-losses on 2022-06-15).
The archived median set remains the documented fallback; any item using it must disclose the statistic.

items.title: CarbonCloud live values used in derived food factors

source.name: CarbonCloud ClimateHub
source.note: CarbonCloud values drift: cheddar moved 18.11 -> 15.09 (-17%) and rolled oats 1.25 -> 1.20 within one research pass. Corroboration-with-access-date only, never a second verification.

watch_for: Standing rule: re-read the live oats input at every data pass and recompute the D3 average.

Prohibition in force: rows dropped as unverifiable (assorted cheeses, chickpeas, potato products, NL tomato, red cabbage, dry onion, oats-UK) must not be resurrected without full product URLs and fresh values.

items.title: Production-share weights inside derived food factors
items.current_value: beef 56% beef-herd / 44% dairy-herd (D6); sugar 80% cane / 20% beet (D8)

source.name: OWID, Less meat or sustainable meat
source.anchor_quote: Around 56% of global beef production comes from dedicated beef herds; and 44% from dairy herds

watch_for: Production shares are not consumption shares -- documented residual; JP consumed beef is ~80% beef-herd via imports.

items.title: Food serving preset weights
items.current_value: FDA RACC (21 CFR 101.12) and USDA FoodData Central portions
watch_for: Japanese product presets (tuna can 70 g, saba can 140 g drained) are manufacturer pages and can 404 on product refresh.

items.title: Appliance per-cycle energy figures
items.current_value: wash 0.350 / 1.300 / 1.700; dryer 4.5 vented, 2.05 heat pump; dishwasher 0.85 eco, 1.12 normal
items.vintage: Bosch EN50229 spec sheets; Which? July 2026

source.name: Bosch manufacturer consumption tables + Which? UK

items.release_cadence: model-dependent; spec sheets disappear when a model is discontinued
watch_for: Manufacturer PDFs are the weak link -- archive them or re-source when a model is retired.
The 'which 60 C?' trap: a label-optimised Eco 60 programme (0.900 kWh) does not reach 60 C, while the user-selected programme (1.700 kWh) does. Keep the same-machine, same-standard pairing.
Appliance efficiency improves steadily; expect downward drift.

items.title: METI measured appliance figures (aircon, TV, heaters, rice cooker)
items.current_value: aircon cooling 0.167679 kWh/h, heating 0.241006; TV 0.079096; rice cooker 0.16 + 0.0165 keep-warm
items.vintage: 省エネルギーセンター実測値 via 資源エネルギー庁; season lengths 暖房期間 169 days / 冷房期間 112 days

source.name: 資源エネルギー庁 省エネポータルサイト

items.release_cadence: irregular; the underlying catalogs are dated 2012-2015
watch_for: PROHIBITION: never 'correct' the aircon values to their JIS catalog ratings (0.435 / 0.455). Measured beats rated; a sanity pin guards this.
If METI republishes with new season lengths, the per-hour derivation changes even if the annual savings do not.
METI's own grid coefficient on that page (0.488 general, 0.429 lighting/TV) is a separate JP figure -- do not confuse it with the house factor.

items.title: Japan national grid coefficient (代替値)
files: reference only -- not shipped; used for JP context copy
items.current_value: 429 g CO2/kWh (令和6年提出用代替値); 416 (61 utilities FY2024-25)

source.name: 環境省 / 資源エネルギー庁 電気事業者別排出係数

watch_for: Becomes a shipped value if regionalisation proceeds (Plan/PDR_GRID_REGIONALISATION.md).

items.title: Household standby power

source.name: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Standby Power
source.anchor_quote: Most products draw relatively little standby power - less than 0.5 watts - but they still add up... Together these amount to 5-10% of residential electricity use.

watch_for: The mechanism matters as much as the number: per-device draw fell 10-30x while device counts rose faster, leaving the household total roughly flat. Copy must reflect that, not 'standby is trivial'.

items.title: Impact equivalency conversion factors
items.current_value: trees 21000 g; carKm 162.72 g; phoneCharges 8 g; burgers 11000 g

source.name: US EPA Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator

items.release_cadence: EPA updates periodically; the mirrored values move whenever their source dataset does
watch_for: THIS FILE IS WHERE DRIFT HIDES. Two of its four values mirror other datasets and must be reconciled every pass, not just re-sourced.
carKm must equal the average petrol car in transport_modes.json.
burgers must equal the beef factor in food_items.json x 113 g.
phoneCharges should agree with the energy dataset's phone_charge entry.
items.reference: see known_drift entries eq_burgers and eq_phone

items.title: Daily eco facts (366 entries)

source.name: mixed tier-1 (IEA 23, OWID 21, UNEP 20, Nature 18, FAO 13, WRAP 11, DOE 11, EST 10, EPA 8, WHO 6)

items.release_cadence: sources republish on their own schedules
watch_for: Facts phrased with a year ('as of 2024...') age visibly and are the priority sweep.
Facts quoting a superlative ('the largest...', 'the fastest-growing...') can silently become false.
Facts whose numbers derive from the food or transport datasets must be reconciled, not just re-sourced.
Dead sourceUrl links -- run a link check as part of the pass.

items.title: Global SDG state assessment
watch_for: This document is explicitly a dated snapshot -- the whole file is a yearly refresh, not a spot-check.
Every claim carries a verbatim quote; the quotes must be re-verified against the new report, not just the numbers swapped.

items.title: UN international observance days
items.release_cadence: the UN adds observances by resolution, irregularly
watch_for: New observances relevant to sustainability; occasional date changes; official page URLs moving.

known_drift.what: impact_equivalencies.json burgers = 11000 g, which encodes the retired beef-herd 99.48 kg CO2e/kg value.
known_drift.should_be: food_items.json ships beef at 70.3608 (decision D6), so a 113 g patty is 7951 g. The file is 38% high.
known_drift.extra: Its own sourceName still claims '113 g beef patty at the 99.48 kg CO2e/kg global mean, matches food_items.json' -- it no longer matches.

known_drift.should_be: The energy research derives 7.0 g at the E1 factor (12.98 Wh battery / 0.85 charge efficiency x 458 g/kWh).

known_drift.what: AUDIT_ACTION_DATA.md section 8 derives the grid factor as 'midpoint of US 370g and UK 210g, biased toward global average'. That midpoint is 290, not the 386 it claimed.
known_drift.should_be: Replace with the E1 derivation: Ember GER 2026, 458 g CO2e/kWh, 2025 data.

known_drift.what: co2_actions_database.json metadata still lists grid_factors us_average 0.37 / uk_average 0.21 from the January 2026 pass, alongside a note recommending per-region user input.
known_drift.should_be: Reconcile with E1. The regionalisation note is not wrong -- it is now tracked in Plan/PDR_GRID_REGIONALISATION.md.

pending_from_decisions.status: decided, not yet applied to data files
changes: data/seed/co2_actions_database.json: air_dry_clothes 1700 -> 2000; cold_water_laundry 600 -> 430; unplug_standby 9 -> 5; led_vs_incandescent 19 -> 23; electric_vs_gasoline_car recompute
re-seed actionLibrary (node scripts/seed/seed_action_library.js, needs the Firebase service account)
re-derive transport sanity pins involving car_bev
pending_from_decisions.points_impact: +7.08% uniformly for affected actions, often 0 after integer rounding. The seeder uses co2Grams^0.4 (CO2_EXPONENT = 0.4), and (co2 x r)^0.4 = co2^0.4 x r^0.4, so the ratio is independent of action size.

pending_from_decisions.status: seeder code synced, re-seed not yet run
pending_from_decisions.note: Bundle with the E1 re-seed -- one seeding operation, not two.

stable_do_not_rechase.why: A fixed published study. Only OWID's processing of it can change, not the study.
Specific heat of water 4.186 kJ/kg-K; latent heat; the 0.09883611 kWh floor to boil 1 L from 15 C. These do not age. Only the surrounding assumptions (flow rate, delta-T, appliance efficiency) can.
Regulatory, changes on a decade timescale.
Fixed by UN resolution through 2030. The indicator DATA moves annually; the targets do not.
Standards revise on multi-year cycles; the measured efficiencies derived from them are stable.
